newsitem.title: UK: Shell reaffirms commitment to Nigeria LNG project.
newsitem.headline: Shell reaffirms commitment to Nigeria LNG project.

text.p: Shell has reaffirmed its commitment to the Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) project despite a furious attack on the company by Oil Minister Dan Etete on Thursday, a company spokesman said.
"Quite obviously Shell, as shareholders in the Nigerian LNG project, is happy to confirm its commitment to the project," he said.
"We would not want to say any more at this stage until we have had time to study more fully what the minister has said and to talk to the minister about it.
"I don't think there has been any formal meeting with him at this stage. We shall obviously be seeking discussions on the matter," the spokesman added, but declined to say more.

Etete, who sacked the board of directors of the Nigerian LNG Limited (NLNG) last month, on Thursday accused Shell Gas BV, the technical leader in the joint venture, of using its position as an independent technical adviser "to subject other shareholders to its whims and caprices."

The government had made concessions to Shell in view of the company's expertise in the gas business, he said, and added Shell was exploiting these concessions "to marginalise government's interest in the project."

He also said measures to involve Nigerians more closely in the project had not been put in place as agreed, called for the shareholder agreement to be reviewed, and said the management of the company would now report directly to the oil ministry.
The four shareholders in the project are state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Agip SpA.

NLNG has set 1999 as the date when gas will be delivered, but has already suffered several postponements and management changes. But last month NLNG said the project was slightly ahead of schedule and was 40 percent complete.
The project is to produce 7.5 billion cubic metres of gas annually for delivery to customers in Spain, France and Turkey.
The fourth and biggest buyer, Enel of Italy, terminated its contract in December and the issue is now before an arbitration panel in Switzerland.
